data.name: HelpTheme
data.value:
Changes the color of the settings window and the tray icon menu.
**Use system setting** — the window follows the app mode in Windows (Settings → Personalization → Colors) and switches automatically, no restart needed.
The layout hint is always dark.

data.name: HelpEnabled
data.value:
Turn off to stop everything for a while: language switching, text correction, snippets and all other rules. KeyMend stays in the tray and the keys work as usual.
The “Enabled” item in the tray icon menu does the same.

data.name: HelpLog
data.value:
The log is a set of text files, one per day, kept for 7 days. It contains only events, for example “converted 5 chars”. KeyMend never records what you type.
Turn it on if something doesn't work: the log helps find the cause.

data.name: HelpAutostart
data.value:
KeyMend starts in the tray, without a window, when you sign in to Windows, with normal permissions. For this it adds one registry entry (shown in “About”).
This switch is unavailable while “Start with Windows as administrator” is on.

data.name: HelpAdmin
data.value:
Windows protects programs that run as administrator: an ordinary program can't switch the language or fix text in them. For example, Task Manager or the Registry Editor.
If you turn this on, KeyMend starts with administrator rights and can work in all windows. Normal startup is turned off at the same time.
Programs and scripts from your rules are still launched with normal permissions.

data.name: HelpHintEnabled
data.value:
When the language changes, a hint with the layout name briefly appears near the text cursor.
It is shown for any change: keys from rules, Alt+Shift or the taskbar. The hint doesn't get in the way: you can click through it and it doesn't take input.

data.name: HelpHintPosition
data.value:
**Near the cursor, otherwise the mouse** — the hint appears next to the text cursor. Some browsers and consoles don't report where the cursor is; then the hint appears at the mouse pointer.
**Always near the mouse** — the hint always appears at the mouse pointer.

data.name: HelpHintDuration
data.value: How many milliseconds the hint stays on screen: from 200 to 5000 (1000 ms is one second).

data.name: HelpHintOnlyOwn
data.value: The hint appears only if KeyMend itself switched the language. There will be no hint when you switch with Alt+Shift, Win+Space or from the taskbar.

data.name: HelpRulesLead
data.value:
Rules let you switch the language, fix text, launch a program or put the computer to sleep with a key press. A rule can have several steps; they run in order.
Rules don't work in programs from “Exclusions”, or in windows that run as administrator while KeyMend itself runs with normal permissions.

data.name: HelpKeys
data.value:
Click “Record”, then press the keys the rule should react to. There are three kinds:
**A single modifier key.** For example, right Ctrl. The rule runs when you press and immediately release only that key.
**Several modifiers together.** For example, right Ctrl and Shift. You can press them in any order. If during recording you hold one key and, without releasing it, press a second one, you get a “hold Ctrl + Shift” rule: it runs only when Ctrl is already held and you press Shift.
**A combination with a regular key.** For example, Ctrl+Alt+K or F13. The rule runs as soon as you press the combination.
Left and right Ctrl, Shift and Alt are different keys. You can't save a combination that is already used by another rule, or a Windows system shortcut (for example, Alt+Tab).

data.name: HelpTime
data.value:
**Single** — the rule runs if you release the keys within this time. If you held them longer, the key was needed for something else, for example Ctrl+C, and the rule doesn't run.
**Double** — the second press must come within this time.
If the same keys have both a single and a double rule, the single one waits to see whether a second press follows, and runs with that delay.

data.name: HelpWhere
data.value:
**In all programs** — everywhere except the programs in the “Exclusions” section.
**Only in selected programs** — only in windows of the selected programs. The name is the program's file name, for example chrome.exe (you can see it in Task Manager on the “Details” tab).
You can assign different rules to the same keys for different programs.

data.name: HelpSwitchHow
data.value:
**Alternate between two languages** — each press switches to the other language of the pair; if the current language isn't in the pair, the first one is selected.
**Always switch to one language** — for example, English before typing a password.

data.name: HelpCorrectWhat
data.value:
Fixes text typed in the wrong layout.
**Selected text** — select the text and press the keys. **Up to the start of the line** — no selection needed: KeyMend picks up the text from the cursor back to the start of the line.
For example, “Ghbdtn? rfr ltkf&” becomes “Привет, как дела?”. Press the keys again to undo the fix; Ctrl+Z undoes it too.

data.name: HelpCorrectLanguages
data.value:
Which layouts to convert between. KeyMend checks which layout has more letters in the text and converts to the other layout of the pair. For example, “ghbdtn” has more English letters, so you get “привет”.
If both layouts have the same number of letters, the text is considered typed in the current layout and is converted to the other one.

data.name: HelpCorrectSwitchAfter
data.value:
When the text is fixed, KeyMend switches to the language it is now written in and shows the layout hint. You can keep typing right away.
Turn it off if you want to switch the language yourself.

data.name: HelpCorrectMax
data.value: Protects against accidentally converting a large block of text: if there is more text, KeyMend leaves it alone. From 10 to 1,000,000 characters.

data.name: HelpLaunchFile
HelpLaunchType
data.value:
Chosen by the file extension. For example, backup.bat gets “Batch file (.cmd, .bat)”, and .ps1 gets “PowerShell 7”.
PowerShell scripts are launched with the -ExecutionPolicy Bypass parameter.

data.name: HelpLaunchArgs
data.value: What to pass to the program after the file name, as on the command line. For example, /SetOrientation 1 90. Put paths with spaces in quotes: "C:\My Documents\report.txt".

data.name: HelpLaunchWindow
data.value:
**Normal** — as when launched by double-clicking. **Hidden** — for scripts that should work unnoticed. **Minimized** — straight to the taskbar.
Some programs decide for themselves how to show their window.

data.name: HelpLaunchRepeat
data.value:
What to do if you press the keys while the program launched last time is still running:
**Don't launch again** — do nothing and let it keep running. The right choice in most cases.
**Launch another copy** — open a second copy next to the first.
**Close it and launch again** — stop the previous one and start over.

data.name: HelpLaunchWait
data.value: The next step of the rule starts only after the program closes. If it ends with an error, a notification appears and the remaining steps don't run.

data.name: HelpLaunchWorkDir
data.value:
The folder where the program looks for files given without a full path. For example, a script saves report.txt — with the working folder D:\Reports the file ends up there.
Empty — the file's own folder; that is usually enough.

data.name: HelpPowerAction
data.value: **Sleep** — the computer goes to sleep, everything stays in memory. **Hibernate** — everything is saved to disk and the computer turns off; hibernation must be turned on in Windows. **Shut down** — the computer turns off. **Restart** — the computer restarts. **Lock** — shows the sign-in screen; programs keep running. **Sign out** — all programs close.

data.name: HelpPowerWhen
data.value:
**Now** — immediately.
**In** — sets a timer from 1 minute to 24 hours; a new timer replaces the previous one. A minute before it fires, a countdown with a “Cancel” button appears. You can also cancel the timer in the tray icon menu.

data.name: HelpPowerCountdown
data.value: Before shutting down or restarting, a window with a 10-second countdown and a “Cancel” button appears — in case the keys were pressed by accident.

data.name: HelpPress
data.value: Which keys to press in the active window, for example Ctrl+Enter, Alt+F4 or Win+D. Other KeyMend rules don't react to key presses made by KeyMend itself.

data.name: HelpDelay
data.value: Wait before the next step, for example until a program window opens. From 0 to 60,000 ms (one minute).

data.name: HelpInsertHow
data.value:
**Type it** — KeyMend types the text as if from the keyboard. Works almost everywhere, but long text is typed noticeably slower.
**Via the clipboard** — fast for any text; the previous clipboard contents are restored afterward.

data.name: HelpInsertNewline
data.value:
How KeyMend types line breaks from the “Text” field.
In chats and messengers Enter often sends the message right away: if the text has a line break, the half-typed text may be sent too early.
**Shift+Enter** breaks the line without sending. **Enter** — for programs where Shift+Enter doesn't work.

data.name: HelpServiceAction
data.value: **Pause or resume KeyMend** — turn all features off or back on, like “Enabled” in the tray icon menu. **Open settings** — open the KeyMend settings window. **Cancel power timer** — cancel a timed sleep or shutdown.

data.name: HelpSnipLead
data.value:
KeyMend remembers the last keys you pressed. When they match an abbreviation, it erases the abbreviation and inserts the text.
An abbreviation works in any layout: for example, “gm ” and “пь ” are the same thing. It's handy to end an abbreviation with a space so it doesn't fire inside words.
Snippets don't work in the KeyMend settings window.

data.name: HelpSnipBuffer
data.value: How many recent key presses KeyMend keeps to recognize an abbreviation (20–1000). What you type is kept only in memory and is erased when you switch windows, click the mouse, or press Enter or Esc.

data.name: HelpSnipKeys
data.value: The letters, digits, symbols and space you type. KeyMend remembers keys, not letters, so the abbreviation is shown nearby as it looks in the other layout. For example, “дд ” and “ll ”.

data.name: HelpSnipSecret
data.value:
For passwords and other secrets. The text is stored encrypted by Windows (it can be read only under your user account); only a reference stays in the settings file.
A secret is inserted only via the clipboard, and the previous clipboard contents are restored afterward.

data.name: HelpSnipAfter
data.value: What to press after the text is inserted, for example Ctrl+Enter to send a message.

data.name: HelpExclLead
data.value:
Programs where KeyMend should behave differently: for example, games or remote desktop with their own key combinations. The checkboxes in a row show what still works in that program; with no checkboxes KeyMend does nothing in it.
A program name is its file name, for example mstsc.exe.

data.name: TransferSaveHint
data.value: To move them to another computer

data.name: HelpTransferSave
data.value:
A .keymend file contains rules, snippets, exclusions, layout hint settings and the files from the scripts folder.
Startup and administrator mode are not included: turn them on again on the other computer.

data.name: TransferSecretsHint
data.value: Passwords from snippets, protected with your password

data.name: HelpTransferSecrets
data.value:
Without this checkbox, secret snippets go into the file without their text and will be turned off on the other computer.
With the checkbox, the secret texts are encrypted with a password you make up here. Without it, the secrets in the file can't be opened.
**The password is not stored anywhere.** If you forget it, the secrets from the file can't be recovered.

data.name: TransferPasswordShort
data.value: The password must be at least {0} characters long

data.name: TransferExportFailed
data.value: Couldn't save the file. See the log for details.

data.name: TransferExportTooLarge
data.value: The files in the scripts folder don't fit into one transfer file.

data.name: TransferLoadHint
data.value: Your current settings are saved to a backup first

data.name: HelpTransferLoad
data.value:
You can load a .keymend file or a plain settings.json, for example the starter set.
The file is checked in full first. If it is damaged or was created by a newer version of KeyMend, nothing changes.

data.name: HelpTransferMode
data.value:
**Replace current** — the settings from the file fully take the place of yours: general settings, rules, snippets, exclusions. Script files from the archive overwrite yours with the same names.
**Add to current** — whatever you don't have is added to yours. General settings and script files with the same names stay yours, and identical items aren't duplicated.
If the keys of a rule or snippet match yours, KeyMend asks which one to keep.
